title: Start with the right access
description: Install the collection, select your execution environment, and plan a safe first connection.
markdown:
## What mAI-skills does

mAI-skills is a collection of nine portable agent skills for World Bank staff using mAI Factory with a coding agent. Each skill supplies instructions, local references, and, where available, a starter or helper. Installing a skill does not grant access, issue credentials, install an mAI service, or change Bank policy. You need approved access, network, runtime, dependencies, and data use.

## Install and invoke

From the project where you use your coding agent, with Git, npm, and Node.js 22.20.0 or later:

```bash
npx skills@1.7.4 add randrescastaneda/mAI-skills --list
npx skills@1.7.4 add randrescastaneda/mAI-skills
```

Select your agent and the skills you need. Each skill is self-contained; the other eight are not required. See [installation options](/guide/installation/) and [client guidance](/guide/clients/).

```text
Use mai-factory to help me connect from my local IDE. Start with onboarding and confirm which access type I need. Do not request or display secrets.
```

## Select your access path

| Where work runs | Access path | Confirm first |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local IDE, personal notebook, approved JupyterHub | Desktop | Onboarding, approved network, current private SDK, supported WAM setup |
| Backend, deployed application, scheduler | Application | Approved app/ACN, IDs, client secret, scope, APIM subscription, network and grants |
| R/Shiny on internal Posit Connect | Posit Connect | Approved content OAuth integration, protected settings and content permissions |
| Bank Databricks workspace | Databricks | Data Lab provisioning and approved workspace identity |

IFC needs its specific onboarding process. Desktop approval does not establish Application, Connect, or Databricks permissions. Do not put a personal Desktop token in an unattended service.

## Desktop migration

The final cutoff is **November 30, 2026**. Desktop Access has a **50 million token monthly limit**. Request extensions from `itsai_platform_admin@worldbankgroup.org`. Complete Web Access Management (WAM) setup under **Desktop Access** in current [platform documentation](https://ai.worldbank.org/platform/documentation). Use the approved current private `itsai-platform` SDK. The supplied material does not specify an exact SDK release, supported OS list, or OS-specific WAM settings.

Use `DesktopToken().get_token(env="DEV")`, `QA`, or `PROD`. Names with `_DESKTOP` suffixes are retired. Do not add device-code, MSAL device flow, or InteractiveBrowserCredential fallback. Follow the [Python workflow](/guide/python-workflow/) for new installs and locked-SDK upgrades. Application client credentials/scopes/APIM, Connect content OAuth, and Databricks managed identity do not change.

## A safe first connection

1. Inspect the consumer project and select the approved access path and environment.
2. Prepare protected credential storage and run offline configuration checks.
3. After approval, test health as route reachability only.
4. Verify model entitlement and required features, then make one small public-sample request.
5. Record non-secret configuration, dependency versions, schema source, and status.

Foundation generation routes now start at `/maifactory`. Preserve health and task APIs under `/conversationalai/platform`; do not strip the prefix globally. Keep existing models, prompts, and business logic when migrating transport. See [model workflows](/guide/model-workflows/), [configuration](/guide/configuration/), and [troubleshooting](/guide/troubleshooting/).

The original migration inputs are local ignored files, not distributed documentation. Never copy source notebook credentials, personal data, cells, or outputs into project files. Offline tests do not prove WAM readiness or live model access.

title: Install, select, and sync
description: Choose direct skill installation or a Git-backed npm dependency, with explicit activation and removal.
markdown:
## Requirements

Skill installation requires Git, npm, and Node.js 22.20.0 or later. Python, R, uv, private SDK access, and mAI credentials are workflow requirements, not requirements for reading or installing every skill. Use approved package sources and networks.

The source repository is public. The npm package is `@randrescastaneda/mai-skills`, marked `private: true`, and declares `UNLICENSED`. The npm flag prevents accidental registry publication; it does not make GitHub private or grant redistribution rights. No npm registry publication is needed for Git installation. Do not put credentials in an installation URL.

## Direct installation

Run from the consumer project:

```bash
npx skills@1.7.4 add randrescastaneda/mAI-skills --list
npx skills@1.7.4 add randrescastaneda/mAI-skills
```

Select skills and supported agents interactively. To install all nine for Claude Code without prompts:

```bash
npx skills@1.7.4 add randrescastaneda/mAI-skills --skill '*' --agent claude-code --yes
```

Replace `claude-code` with a supported identifier, such as `codex`, `cursor`, `github-copilot`, or `kilo`. Use the pinned CLI's list for current choices. Quotes around `'*'` prevent shell expansion. For a Python first connection:

```bash
npx skills@1.7.4 add randrescastaneda/mAI-skills --skill mai-factory mai-credentials mai-python
```

Project-local installation is the default. Add `--global` for your user account or `--copy` when symlinks are not permitted. Each skill includes its own required references and assets.

## Git-backed npm installation

```bash
npm install --save-dev skills@1.7.4 git+https://github.com/randrescastaneda/mAI-skills.git
npx skills experimental_sync --agent claude-code --yes
```

The explicit sync is required. `npm install` alone does not activate skills. `experimental_sync` is an upstream experimental command pinned through `skills@1.7.4`; it scans installed dependencies and links their skills. Re-run it after updates, especially with copies. If sync is unavailable, use the stable local-path installer:

```bash
npx skills@1.7.4 add ./node_modules/@randrescastaneda/mai-skills --skill '*' --agent claude-code --yes
```

Retain the consumer lock file and pin reviewed Git commits where required. A branch name is not an immutable release. The package is not published to the npm registry; do not use the package name alone as its source.

## Approved package handoff

A maintainer can use `npm pack` and share a trusted archive through an approved channel:

```bash
npm install --save-dev skills@1.7.4 ./randrescastaneda-mai-skills-0.1.0.tgz
npx skills experimental_sync --agent claude-code --yes
```

Use the correct versioned filename. This needs npm dependencies or an approved cache; it is not a fully offline dependency installer. Original source references are excluded from the package.

## Confirm activation

```text
Use mai-factory. Explain which access path fits this project and what you can check offline before I sign in. Do not read or display credentials.
```

Check the selected agent, scope, and installation/sync result if the skill is not found. Client activation behavior varies. See [clients](/guide/clients/) and [updates](/guide/updates/). The third-party CLI has telemetry and security-audit behavior. Review its policy; documented opt-outs are `DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`. Installing these instructions does not upgrade the private Desktop SDK; use the [Python workflow](/guide/python-workflow/) for that step.

title: Use skills in your coding agent
description: Understand the portable format, client selection, and explicit prompts that work without invented slash commands.
markdown:
## The compatibility boundary

The collection uses portable `SKILL.md` instructions. The pinned Skills CLI installs for supported agents; each client decides how it discovers and activates skills. Installation support does not guarantee identical activation, permissions, tools, or execution behavior. These are instructions, not a server, model account, or general ChatGPT connector.

| Client | Example CLI identifier |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `claude-code` |
| Codex | `codex` |
| Cursor | `cursor` |
| GitHub Copilot | `github-copilot` |
| Kilo | `kilo` |

Use the installer list for current choices. Do not assume universal slash commands. Name the skill in a natural-language request.

## Invoke explicitly

```text
Use mai-python to migrate this Desktop client to WAM and root mAI Factory Responses routes. Inspect existing files, keep models and prompts unchanged, and test offline before login. Do not request or display credentials.
```

```text
Use mai-r to configure my approved R workflow. Separate Posit Connect content OAuth from local Desktop WAM access, then check configuration offline.
```

## Match the task

| Task | Starting skill |
| --- | --- |
| New user, access selection or Desktop migration | `mai-factory` |
| Credential types, storage and rotation | `mai-credentials` |
| Python setup or WAM migration | `mai-python` |
| R/Shiny content OAuth or Desktop | `mai-r` |
| Models, embeddings, tools, streaming | `mai-foundation-models` |
| Document search, tagging, translation, speech | `mai-platform-apis` |
| Bulk independent requests | `mai-batch` |
| Managed Bank workspace | `mai-databricks` |
| Safe error diagnosis | `mai-troubleshooting` |

Give the task, language, execution location, environment, approval status, and available non-secret evidence. Do not supply credentials or confidential text.

```text
Use mai-foundation-models. I need embeddings for approved public documents from an Application Access job in DEV. List the schema and model facts that need current verification, then prepare synthetic parser tests. Do not make live calls until access and the contract are confirmed.
```

## When the agent skips a skill

Confirm installation for this client and scope. With npm, check that sync ran after updates. Name the skill and ask the agent to report which instructions it loaded and which offline check it will run. Each skill is standalone; do not assume sibling files exist in a partial install. Keep installed assets separate from editable consumer-project files and inspect the project before copying a starter. Browse the [complete reference](/reference/mai-factory/) for the exact instructions.

title: Your first Python connection
description: Prepare Desktop WAM or Application Access, validate offline, and make an approved root Responses request.
markdown:
## Start with a concrete request

```text
Use mai-python to create or migrate a DEV starter. Use protected credentials, preserve existing models and prompts, and run offline checks before login. Confirm WAM setup and the current model contract.
```

The [Python starter](/reference/mai-python/assets/mai_client/) is a small synchronous learning example for Desktop and Application Access, not a production service, async server, or Databricks installer. Inspect the project before changes and copy/adapt assets into the consumer project, not the installed skill.

## 1. Prepare dependencies

For a new project only:

```bash
uv init --python 3.12
uv add 'openai==3.35.1' requests keyring
```

OpenAI 3.35.1 is the tested client release. Python 3.12 is a historical starter choice, not proof of current WAM SDK compatibility. Confirm current private SDK/runtime/OS requirements in **Desktop Access** documentation. The supplied material gives no exact SDK release, supported OS list, or OS-specific WAM settings.

## 2. Select authentication

Desktop requires onboarding, approved network, the current private SDK, and Web Access Management (WAM) setup under **Desktop Access** in [platform documentation](https://ai.worldbank.org/platform/documentation). Merge the [named private index](/reference/mai-python/assets/desktop-index/) into existing TOML without duplicate tables. Follow [protected index setup](/reference/mai-python/references/setup/); never put JFrog credentials in URLs, lock files, chat, or tool calls. For a new install:

```bash
uv add itsai-platform
```

For an existing uv project, upgrade the lock through the approved authenticated private index:

```bash
uv lock --upgrade-package itsai-platform
uv sync
```

`uv add` alone can retain an older locked release. Check the installed SDK against current Desktop Access requirements before login. Use the real string returned by `DesktopToken().get_token(env="DEV")`, `QA`, or `PROD`. Old `_DESKTOP` suffixes and a supposed SDK `token_provider` method are not valid migration targets. No device-code, MSAL device flow, or InteractiveBrowserCredential fallback.

The final Desktop cutoff is **November 30, 2026**; the monthly limit is **50 million tokens**. Request extensions from `itsai_platform_admin@worldbankgroup.org`.

Application Access is unchanged. Install `azure-identity`, confirm app/ACN approval, environment grants, IDs, client secret, scope and APIM key. Use the approved runtime secret service. Local learning can use the approved OS store under `worldbank-mai/DEV`, with accounts `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET` and `APIM_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY`. The starter reads process environment before that store. A deployed service must not depend on a developer's OS store or personal Desktop login.

## 3. Check offline

```bash
export MAI_ENV=DEV
export MAI_ACCESS_TYPE=desktop
export MAI_TEAM_NAME=your-approved-team-name
uv run python mai_client.py check
```

PowerShell:

```powershell
$env:MAI_ENV = "DEV"
$env:MAI_ACCESS_TYPE = "desktop"
$env:MAI_TEAM_NAME = "your-approved-team-name"
uv run python mai_client.py check
```

For Application Access also configure `MAI_ACCESS_TYPE=application` and approved tenant/client IDs. `check` performs no login, credential-store read, or network call. The starter does not auto-load `.env`.

## 4. Approved health and model tests

After approval, run `uv run python mai_client.py health`. This obtains a provider token and uses a 30-second timeout with redirects disabled. Health remains at `/conversationalai/platform/health/` and proves route reachability only.

Set `MAI_OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://azapimdev.worldbank.org/maifactory/openai/` for DEV and `MAI_MODEL` to the approved existing model. Use the matched QA/PROD host only with approval. The trailing slash is required; the SDK appends `responses`. The retired foundation root below `/conversationalai/maifactory` is rejected. Model entitlement and optional features still need current verification.

```bash
uv run python mai_client.py ask --prompt "Reply with the single word: pong"
```

The request uses Responses, model in JSON, and at most 128 output tokens. Use token controls only on supported models; omit GPT-5 `temperature` and add `reasoning` only when supported. Keep business logic unchanged. The explicit `ask` command displays response text, so use only public text in CLI arguments.

## Refresh and extraction

Tokens last about one hour. OpenAI 3.35.1 supports the starter's `api_key` callable, which returns an actual `get_token` string per request. This is a local wrapper, not a DesktopToken SDK method. Rebuild any client that captured a string after refresh; Gemini captures both `api_key` and Authorization. Raw HTTP obtains fresh headers before each request.

OpenAI `output_text` may be empty. The starter also extracts structured output text, without a fixed output index, and fails safely when no text is present. Keep retries off initially and never log raw responses or exception bodies. Record dependency versions, source/date, offline result, and approved test status, not credentials or notebook output. Offline tests do not prove native WAM support or live model access.

title: Connect R and Shiny
description: Keep Posit Connect content OAuth or use approved Desktop WAM, then test the root Responses transport.
markdown:
## Name the runtime first

```text
Use mai-r to configure my approved R workflow. Keep credentials outside the repository. Separate Posit Connect OAuth from Desktop WAM, explain token expiry, and check configuration offline.
```

The [R starter](/reference/mai-r/assets/mai_client/) supports `posit-connect` and `desktop`. An unattended backend outside Connect needs approved Application Access and its provider, not another mode in this starter. Databricks R uses workspace instructions.

## Posit Connect content OAuth

The Desktop migration does not change approved internal Connect content OAuth. Confirm the content's mAI integration, target environment/audience, and permissions. This documented flow does not require Desktop onboarding. Set `API_KEY` and `OAUTH_INTEGRATION_GUID` through protected content settings. The key authenticates to Connect; it is not an mAI bearer, APIM subscription, or public OpenAI key. The GUID identifies the integration. Never put actual values in R source or agent chat.

Install from an approved source and copy/adapt the starter into the consumer project:

```r
install.packages(c("connectapi", "httr2"))
source("mai_client.R")
Sys.setenv(MAI_ACCESS_TYPE = "posit-connect", MAI_ENV = "DEV",
           MAI_TEAM_NAME = "your-approved-team-name", MAI_SOURCE_TYPE = "interactive")
config <- mai_config()
```

Configuration performs no login, credential-store read, or network request. The provider checks protected Connect settings when it obtains credentials. The starter does not auto-load `.env`.

## Local Desktop WAM

Confirm Desktop approval, network, and Web Access Management (WAM) setup under **Desktop Access** in platform documentation. Use the approved current private Python SDK. No exact SDK release, supported OS list, or OS-specific WAM settings were supplied. Python 3.12 is a historical starter choice, not a current support guarantee. Follow [private SDK setup](/guide/python-workflow/). In an existing uv project, use `uv lock --upgrade-package itsai-platform` and `uv sync` through the approved authenticated index; `uv add` can retain an old lock.

Bind `reticulate` before Python initializes:

```r
install.packages("reticulate")
reticulate::use_virtualenv("/path/to/approved/.venv", required = TRUE)
Sys.setenv(MAI_ACCESS_TYPE = "desktop", MAI_ENV = "DEV",
           MAI_TEAM_NAME = "your-approved-team-name", MAI_SOURCE_TYPE = "interactive")
config <- mai_config()
provider <- mai_token_provider(config)
```

The provider uses `DesktopToken().get_token(env="DEV")`, `QA`, or `PROD`, not retired `_DESKTOP` names or an SDK `token_provider` method. No device-code, MSAL device flow, or InteractiveBrowserCredential fallback. Do not save a bearer in `.Renviron` or make static keyring storage a new login default.

The final Desktop cutoff is **November 30, 2026**. The monthly limit is **50 million tokens**; request extensions from `itsai_platform_admin@worldbankgroup.org`. Tokens last about one hour. The HTTP wrapper acquires through the provider per request; clients that capture a string need refresh and rebuild.

## Health and Responses

After approval:

```r
provider <- mai_token_provider(config)
mai_health(config, provider)
```

The starter uses TLS verification, a 30-second timeout, no redirects, no automatic retries, and sanitized errors. Health stays at `/conversationalai/platform/health/` and establishes reachability only.

The canonical full DEV endpoint is `https://azapimdev.worldbank.org/maifactory/openai/responses`. Set `MAI_RESPONSES_URL` to that full URL and `MAI_MODEL` to the approved existing model through non-secret configuration. R needs the full endpoint; Python needs the SDK base with trailing slash. The old foundation route is rejected. Confirm entitlement and optional features before calling.

```r
config <- mai_config()
text <- mai_ask(config, provider, "Reply with the single word: pong")
```

Responses sends model in JSON. The wrapper requests at most 128 output tokens and reads non-empty `output_text` or structured output text, not legacy `choices`. Omit GPT-5 `temperature`; use output-token/reasoning controls only when supported. Preserve models, prompts and business logic.

## Shiny and migration

Keep user/session chat state separate. A cached bare token in a global or reactive value does not refresh itself. Confirm Connect's current long-session behavior and permissions. Show safe errors rather than raw request objects or bodies. Verify ellmer version, approved route, and refresh support before configuring it; do not set `OPENAI_API_KEY` to the Connect key. See [migration boundaries](/reference/mai-r/references/migration/). Offline tests do not verify WAM, live model grants, or Connect integration readiness.

title: Prepare and reconcile a batch
description: Validate a structural JSONL fixture offline, then use bounded monitoring and complete result reconciliation.
markdown:
## When batch fits

Use batch for independent bulk requests when latency permits it, such as reviewing approved public abstracts with stable non-sensitive IDs. Confirm access, environment, team, data classification, job size, and model. Scheduled workers use approved unattended identity, not a personal Desktop token.

```text
Use mai-batch to prepare a small public-sample batch. Validate JSONL offline, list missing contract facts, and design bounded monitoring, reconciliation, and retention. Do not submit before access and schema verification.
```

## 1. Verify the batch contract

The migration guide resolves synchronous OpenAI generation to root `/maifactory/openai/`. It does not verify every files/batches route, supported per-record target, body feature, completion window, state, limit, or retention parameter. Get those from current mAI documentation, not an upstream example or retired `/conversationalai/v2` batch route. Keep models, prompts, and business logic unchanged.

The JSONL record `url` must equal the batch creation `endpoint` exactly. `/chat/completions`, `/v1/chat/completions`, and `/v1/responses` are not interchangeable. Change payload and parser with the target; do not rename only the URL.

## 2. Validate offline

This is a structural fixture, not a verified sendable request:

```jsonl
{"custom_id":"task-001","method":"POST","url":"/v1/responses","body":{"model":"VERIFIED_BATCH_DEPLOYMENT","input":"Public test sentence."}}
{"custom_id":"task-002","method":"POST","url":"/v1/responses","body":{"model":"VERIFIED_BATCH_DEPLOYMENT","input":"Another public test sentence."}}
```

Save each object on one physical UTF-8 line. With Python 3.10 or later, use the [offline validator](/reference/mai-batch/scripts/validate_jsonl/):

```bash
python /path/to/installed/mai-batch/scripts/validate_jsonl.py input.jsonl \
  --endpoint /v1/responses --model VERIFIED_BATCH_DEPLOYMENT
```

Use the actual installed path. The validator has no third-party dependencies or network calls. It rejects empty files, blank lines, malformed JSON, duplicate keys, non-finite values, wrong methods/targets/models, and duplicate or blank IDs. Success exits 0; failure exits 2 with static reasons and line numbers. It does not verify body schemas, deployment, policy, token counts, access, quota, or live limits.

## 3. Submit with durable state

1. Save environment, verified target/model, source/date, input digest, count, non-sensitive IDs, and state in an approved manifest.
2. Apply current limits and pricing; do not promise historical discounts or completion windows.
3. Upload with the verified purpose, content type, processing and retention settings; save the input file ID.
4. Create with the exact canonical target; save the batch ID immediately.
5. Monitor and download with the same identity/environment and fresh credentials.

Desktop WAM uses `get_token(env="DEV")`, `QA`, or `PROD`; follow the [access reference](/reference/mai-batch/references/access-and-verification/) for setup, SDK upgrades, cutoff and monthly limit. Application, Connect, and Databricks identity do not change. Tokens expire, so long monitoring cannot depend on a string captured once. Include Authorization, actual `x-source-type`, approved team attribution, and required app subscription headers on every operation.

## 4. Monitor with a stopping rule

Set both a monotonic deadline and maximum attempts. Poll at least 60 seconds apart, or a longer platform requirement or `Retry-After`. Verify current states and investigate unknown states. A local timeout does not cancel a remote job. Save state and IDs, stop, and resume by ID. Monitoring is not resubmission. Investigate ambiguous upload/create timeouts before retries to avoid duplicate jobs and cost.

## 5. Reconcile every input

Download available output and error files at documented terminal states. Match by `custom_id`, never line position. Account for successful, failed, missing, duplicate, and unknown IDs. A completed job can contain failed requests; failed or expired jobs may contain useful partial results. Save accepted successes once. Retry only eligible failures with lineage to the original manifest. Apply bounded retries only to confirmed transient failures. Track retention, retrieval deadlines and deletion for all artifacts. Expired download credentials do not prove file deletion. Never log tokens, full headers, SAS URLs or payloads.

title: Build a verified model integration
description: Use the resolved foundation routes while preserving provider schemas, token refresh, models, and prompts.
markdown:
## Migrate transport, not business logic

```text
Use mai-foundation-models to migrate this approved DEV client. Keep existing prompts, models, and application logic. Use the resolved foundation routes, verify model features and entitlement, and test serialization and parsing offline before any live request.
```

The supplied migration guide resolves ordinary generation routes. It does not verify every tool, stream, embedding, grounding feature, or deployment entitlement. Record source/date, access path, environment, full URL or SDK composition, model, headers, request/response shape, supported features, and limits. Check the [current model catalog](https://ai.worldbankgroup.org/maifactory/). Do not replace a model just because a source example uses another name.

## Canonical DEV transport

| Provider | Base and operation | Native contract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenAI | `https://azapimdev.worldbank.org/maifactory/openai/`, SDK appends `responses` | Model in JSON, `instructions` and `input`, structured output |
| Gemini | `https://azapimdev.worldbank.org/maifactory/gemini` plus `/responses/{model}` or `/models/{model}:generateContent` | Native `contents` and `parts`, optional `systemInstruction` and `generationConfig` |
| Bedrock | `https://azapimdev.worldbank.org/maifactory/bedrock/model/{model_id}/converse` | Raw HTTP Converse, model in path |

Use the matching QA/PROD host only when approved. The old `/conversationalai/maifactory` foundation root is retired. Preserve `/conversationalai/platform` for health and task services. Never strip prefixes globally or send to a public provider as a fallback.

## OpenAI Responses

Use `OpenAI`, not the retired Azure deployment Chat Completions transport. Keep the trailing slash on the SDK base; raw HTTP uses the full `/maifactory/openai/responses` URL. Test the `messages` to `instructions`/`input` mapping and `choices` to structured output parser together. Omit GPT-5 `temperature`; use `max_output_tokens` and `reasoning` only if supported by the selected model.

Prefer non-empty `output_text`, then read text from `output[].content[].text` without a fixed index. Text convenience fields can be empty. Handle tools, refusals, incomplete states and no text safely; do not dump raw responses. See the [Python](/guide/python-workflow/) and [R](/guide/r-workflow/) starters.

## Native Gemini

For `google-genai`, set the base to `/maifactory/gemini`, set `api_version=""`, and put the bearer string in both `api_key` and Authorization. The empty version prevents an inserted `/v1beta/` and APIM 404. Rebuild after token refresh at about one hour. Keep existing generation controls under `generationConfig`; `max_tokens` maps to `maxOutputTokens`. Read `candidates[].content.parts[].text` or SDK `.text`, with safety/empty-candidate handling. Do not send OpenAI `input` or chat `messages` to native generation. Do not bypass APIM with GCP ADC.

Grounding/Interactions is separate. Verify the exact current contract for an existing grounded client; do not enable it during a transport-only generation migration. Only if the old client already uploaded files, verify DEV/QA helpers under `/maifactory/gemini/gcs/uploads` and native `fileData.fileUri` with `gs://` URIs. Do not introduce uploads or OpenAI `input_file` blocks.

## Bedrock Converse

Use raw HTTP, such as `requests`, through APIM. Do not use boto3/botocore SigV4. Use `messages[].content[].text`, `system` text blocks, and `inferenceConfig.maxTokens`. Do not send `anthropic_version`, native `max_tokens`, or typed Anthropic blocks. Parse `output.message.content[].text` and camelCase usage fields such as `inputTokens` and `outputTokens`. Keep the approved model ID in the path. Confirm the current US residency allowlist and inference profile; a `us.` prefix alone does not prove approval.

## Authentication and bounded features

Desktop now uses WAM and `DesktopToken().get_token(env="DEV")`, `QA`, or `PROD`. Follow the [standalone access reference](/reference/mai-foundation-models/references/access-and-verification/) for setup, upgrades, cutoff and monthly limit. No device-code fallback. Application client credentials/scopes/APIM, Connect OAuth, and Databricks managed identity do not change.

Every call needs Authorization, actual `x-source-type`, approved team attribution, and any required subscription key. Tokens last about one hour. The tested OpenAI 3.35.1 callable returns the actual token string per request; it is not a DesktopToken SDK method. Other clients need a verified refresh hook or rebuild after a captured string is refreshed.

Verify LangChain conversion and callable support before `use_responses_api=True`. For embeddings, verify route, dimensions, model/version/task, limits and ordering; keep stable IDs and protected vectors. For tools, use strict schemas, an allowlist, resource authorization, bounded rounds and approval for changes or export. A model request is not permission to execute. For streaming, verify the provider-specific framing, final state, errors and usage; close on cancellation and do not blindly replay partial streams. Use timeouts, bounded concurrency and one retry layer. Never log payloads, credentials or SAS URLs. Browse the [complete reference](/reference/mai-foundation-models/) for the remaining verification checks.

title: Search, translate, tag, and synthesize
description: Preserve platform routes and use reviewed schemas, bounded processing, and retained source evidence.
markdown:
## Preserve the platform boundary

```text
Use mai-platform-apis to design a public-document workflow in DEV. Verify DNR search and response schemas, prepare pagination and parser tests offline, and retain source IDs and citations. Do not call until access and the contract are confirmed.
```

The foundation migration does not remove `/conversationalai/platform` from health, Documents & Reports, tagging, translation, or text-to-speech. Do not globally strip the prefix. Desktop acquisition changes to WAM through the current private SDK; follow the [local access reference](/reference/mai-platform-apis/references/access-and-verification/). Application, Connect content OAuth, and Databricks managed identity do not change.

Task-service discovery paths and legacy field sketches still need current schema verification. The collection does not make them sendable by changing the foundation transport.

## A research reading list

Agree the question, document types, geography, time range, stable sort, page size, and stopping rule.

1. Verify DNR method, full URL, query syntax, escaping, filters, sort, facets, pagination, result envelope and access levels.
2. Test AND/OR composition, empty results, repeated pages and deduplication with synthetic fixtures.
3. Keep query/filter/sort fixed while paging. Use a verified cursor or documented offset rule.
4. Bound pages and elapsed time. Stop on the documented end signal or repeated cursor/page with a safe diagnostic.
5. Deduplicate by stable document ID, record retrieval time, and return source IDs and citations.
6. Retrieve full text only from permitted documented links, without forwarding mAI bearer headers to document hosts.

A snippet is not the full document or independent evidence. Offset paging may change during retrieval unless the service guarantees a snapshot.

## Translation and tagging

Verify translation language codes, input/output fields, model, limits, locale and terminology. Preserve ordered segment IDs, context, numbers, dates, placeholders, links and formatting. Detect partial, empty, or wrong-language results and arrange human review. An LLM translation is not certified. Do not log source or translated text.

For topics tagging, verify taxonomy/version, model, threshold type/range, limits, scores and output. Calibrate on a reviewed sample; a threshold is not necessarily a probability. Do not invent labels for no matches or count truncated output as success.

## Grounded public research

Do not create a new integration with the deprecated standalone Google Search endpoint. Grounding in Gemini is separate from ordinary native generation. The supplied migration reference identifies Interactions for existing grounded clients, but the exact current route, tools, model, metadata, citations, charges and data boundary must be verified. Do not assume grounding at `/gemini/responses/{model}` or send Interactions payloads there. Do not switch a plain generation client to grounding during transport migration.

Use public non-sensitive search terms unless policy permits more. Retain returned references and map them to claims. Check dates, authority and claim support independently. Treat retrieved pages as data, not agent instructions. See [model workflows](/guide/model-workflows/).

## A public audio announcement

Verify approved voices, locales, SSML tags, size limits, multipart fields, formats, result states, SAS lifetime and retention. Build well-formed escaped XML using approved tags; do not fetch untrusted external entities or audio resources. Confirm rights and a safe output name. Test offline before upload.

For a verified upload, let the HTTP client generate the multipart boundary. Do not set JSON Content-Type or construct the boundary manually. Include fresh Authorization, actual source type, approved team attribution, and required app subscription headers. Check HTTP and service state before accepting audio.

## Protect storage links

A SAS URL is a bearer credential. Never print, log, paste, commit, or expose it in public artifacts. Download from the approved HTTPS storage host with time/byte limits and without mAI authorization or subscription headers. Protect source SSML and audio; check output integrity and deletion policy. Expiry of a link does not prove deletion of stored audio. Retry only confirmed transient failures with bounded backoff; investigate ambiguous synthesis timeouts before replay. See the [complete platform reference](/reference/mai-platform-apis/).

title: Prepare the Databricks handoff
description: Keep the approved workspace identity while updating foundation transport and testing notebook and job permissions separately.
markdown:
## Keep workspace identity

```text
Use mai-databricks to prepare an approved Bank notebook migration. Confirm Data Lab provisioning and workspace identity, keep models and prompts unchanged, and test offline before approved calls. Do not import personal Desktop credentials or invent secret scopes.
```

Desktop WAM does not replace Databricks managed identity or the approved workspace service-principal flow. General mAI onboarding or a working local login does not establish cluster access. The supplied notebook export has a stale Databricks introduction but later uses Desktop authentication. It does not authorize personal Desktop login on a cluster. Never copy its credential-like installation data, personal information, cells, or outputs.

## 1. Confirm provisioning

Identify workspace, cluster/runtime, team, environment, interactive or scheduled work, classification, and approved use. Use Data Lab Services and the Data Science workspace team. IFC also needs its specific process. Obtain current runtime/package, network, identity, endpoint, model and header instructions. The sources do not specify a workspace token acquisition API. Do not invent `dbutils.secrets` scopes, Spark settings, serving names, or managed-identity helpers.

## 2. Prepare without secrets

Inspect the notebook/project and create synthetic request/response fixtures. Do not run the local private-index installer or personal WAM/Desktop login on a shared cluster. Keep personal bearers, JFrog tokens, application secrets and APIM keys out of cells, widgets, output, Spark configuration, and committed notebooks. Redaction is not permission for unrestricted logs.

## 3. Update transport only

Foundation generation now uses root `/maifactory`: OpenAI `/openai/responses`, native Gemini `/gemini/responses/{model}` or `/gemini/models/{model}:generateContent`, and Bedrock `/bedrock/model/{model_id}/converse`. Preserve health and task APIs under `/conversationalai/platform`. Do not combine retired paths and new bodies or change models, prompts and business logic.

OpenAI's SDK base ends `/maifactory/openai/`; model goes in JSON. Handle empty `output_text` with structured output text extraction. Omit GPT-5 `temperature`; use output-token/reasoning controls only when supported. Gemini uses native `contents`/`parts`, empty `google-genai` `api_version`, bearer in both `api_key` and Authorization, and client rebuild after refresh. Grounding/Interactions needs separate verification. Bedrock uses raw HTTP Converse, not Anthropic native fields or boto3/SigV4 through APIM.

Match DEV/QA/PROD host and scope. Include Authorization, approved `x-team-name`, actual `x-source-type=interactive` or `job`, and the subscription key when the workspace Application contract requires it. Use the workspace provider's refresh policy. Rebuild clients that captured token strings after refresh; do not persist a notebook bearer as a reusable key.

## 4. Verify separate identities

1. Check non-secret configuration and synthetic serialization/parsing offline.
2. After approval, test documented health with TLS and a finite timeout; interpret reachability only.
3. Confirm current model permissions and optional features with documentation or the workspace team's approved example. If unavailable, request a non-secret excerpt.
4. Make one small public-sample call and record status, request ID, environment, model, versions and UTC time.
5. Test scheduled-job identity separately; notebook success does not prove job access.

## Handoff

Return provisioning status, unresolved identity/contract facts, offline checks, approved network/auth status and job-identity status. Share only permitted workspace identifiers, sanitized error category, timestamp, versions and request ID with the responsible team. Do not disable TLS or use a public provider workaround. Browse the [Databricks reference](/reference/mai-databricks/) and [troubleshooting](/reference/mai-troubleshooting/) for support channels.

title: Configure without exposing secrets
description: Match hosts, current Desktop environment names, exact foundation routes, workload headers, and credential refresh.
markdown:
## Separate configuration and credentials

The Python settings template is a configuration inventory and supplies the canonical DEV base. Neither starter auto-loads `.env`. Set non-secret values in the runtime or approved configuration system; put secrets in approved local OS stores or runtime secret services. An ignored file is still readable by tools.

```text
Use mai-credentials to review this project's setting names, access type, environment and rotation owner. Do not read, display, or request secret values.
```

## Common settings

| Setting | Purpose | Starter behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MAI_ENV` | DEV, QA, PROD | Both default to DEV and reject unknown names |
| `MAI_ACCESS_TYPE` | Approved access path | Python: desktop/application; R: desktop/posit-connect |
| `MAI_TEAM_NAME` | Approved team attribution | Both require a non-empty ASCII header value |
| `MAI_MODEL` | Exact approved deployment | Required for model request; do not invent a model |
| `MAI_OPENAI_BASE_URL` | Python SDK base | Exact matched-host `/maifactory/openai/` with trailing slash |
| `MAI_RESPONSES_URL` | R full endpoint | Exact matched-host `/maifactory/openai/responses` |
| `MAI_SOURCE_TYPE` | Actual interactive or job work | R and general scaffolds use it; Python derives local/app defaults |

Python uses `interactive` for Desktop and `job` for Application. Adapt deliberately for another approved workload; the header is not a way to change priority, timeout or quota.

## Match the environment

| Environment | Host | Desktop `get_token` environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DEV | `azapimdev.worldbank.org` | `DEV` |
| QA | `azapimqa.worldbank.org` | `QA` |
| PROD | `azapim.worldbank.org` | `PROD` |

The old `_DESKTOP` suffixes are retired. Use the approved current private SDK and Web Access Management (WAM) setup from **Desktop Access** documentation. No exact SDK version, supported OS list, or OS-specific WAM settings were supplied. See [Python setup and upgrade](/guide/python-workflow/). No device-code, MSAL device flow or InteractiveBrowserCredential fallback. The Desktop cutoff is **November 30, 2026**, with **50 million tokens per month**; extensions go to `itsai_platform_admin@worldbankgroup.org`.

Application scopes are unchanged; use the matched row from the [credential reference](/reference/mai-credentials/). Keep host, scope, subscription, grants and deployment matched. DEV approval is not QA/PROD approval. Neither starter accepts public providers or arbitrary scope overrides. Foundation root routes replace the old `/conversationalai/maifactory` family. Keep `/conversationalai/platform` for health and task APIs.

## Other access paths are unchanged

`AZURE_TENANT_ID` and `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` come from the app owner. `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET` and `APIM_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY` are secrets. Python reads them from process environment first, then an approved OS store under `worldbank-mai/DEV`, QA, or PROD. Deployed services use Key Vault or the approved secret service, not a developer's store. Vault access is separate from mAI entitlement.

Connect content settings `API_KEY` and `OAUTH_INTEGRATION_GUID` remain with the approved content OAuth flow. The key authenticates to Connect, not mAI. Confirm environment, audience, integration grants and long-session behavior. Databricks keeps its provisioned workspace identity.

## Headers and refresh

Every call needs Authorization, actual `x-source-type` and approved team attribution per onboarding; the starters require `x-team-name`. Application Access still uses `Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key`. Use JSON Content-Type for JSON and let the client set multipart boundaries. Never put tokens in query strings or forward credential headers across hosts.

Desktop tokens last about one hour. OpenAI 3.35.1 supports a callable returning the actual `get_token` string per request. The wrapper is not an SDK `token_provider` method. A string captured at construction does not refresh itself: refresh and rebuild such clients. Gemini captures bearer in both `api_key` and Authorization and needs rebuild; `google-genai` also needs `api_version=""`. Raw HTTP obtains fresh headers immediately before each request. See [security](/guide/security/) and the [Python](/reference/mai-python/assets/mai_client/) and [R](/reference/mai-r/assets/mai_client/) implementations.

title: Diagnose one layer at a time
description: Separate installation, WAM setup, network, access, transport, parsing and quota failures with safe evidence.
markdown:
## Start with safe evidence

```text
Use mai-troubleshooting to isolate this failure. Separate network, WAM/auth, authorization, schema, parsing, and quota checks. Change one variable at a time. Do not request tokens, raw traces, headers, or payloads.
```

If credentials or SAS links were exposed, stop sharing and follow revocation/rotation and incident procedures. Deleting a log does not invalidate a credential.

## Installation and setup

Check Git/npm/Node.js 22.20.0 or later for skill installation, the selected client and scope for activation, and the explicit npm sync step. Re-sync copied installs after updates. A skill update does not upgrade `itsai-platform`.

Desktop requires the approved current private SDK and Web Access Management (WAM) setup under **Desktop Access** documentation. For existing uv projects, use protected private-index authentication, `uv lock --upgrade-package itsai-platform`, then `uv sync`. `uv add` can keep an old lock. No exact SDK release, supported OS list, or OS-specific WAM configuration was supplied. Do not guess them or add device-code, MSAL device flow, or InteractiveBrowserCredential fallback.

Use `get_token(env="DEV")`, `QA`, or `PROD`, not retired `_DESKTOP` names. A JFrog token downloads the private SDK; it is not a model key. R must bind reticulate before Python initializes. Neither starter auto-loads `.env`.

## Interpret evidence narrowly

Health remains under `/conversationalai/platform/health/`. Success proves reachability for that route, not onboarding, token validity, complete app grants or model entitlement. A health failure does not prove all inference backends are down. Use approved hostname-only network diagnostics for failures before HTTP. Preserve TLS, MFA, VPN and permission controls. Confirm current network policy and any Mac or IFC process with support.

| Status | Check | Safe action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | Missing/expired bearer, tenant, matched host/scope, credential expiry | Correct cause and obtain a fresh token before retry |
| 403 | User/app/product/model grants, subscription and network/ACN | Confirm provisioning with the owner |
| 404 | Canonical route, environment, model and SDK suffix/version | Correct complete URL composition |
| 400/422 | Protocol, field names/types, model controls, multipart/JSON | Validate schema before another request |
| 429 | RPM/TPM throttle, upstream quota, budget and reset evidence | Bound backoff for transient limits; stop for exhausted quota |
| 500 | Backend/gateway or parser mismatch | Use sanitized ID/time; retry only confirmed transient errors |
| 504 | Remote deadline and possible accepted operation | Reconcile before replay |

A status alone is not a diagnosis. Locally review only a small sanitized category.

## Migration-specific checks

OpenAI SDK base must end `/maifactory/openai/`; it appends `responses`. Do not send Chat Completions to it. Model goes in JSON. The old `/conversationalai/maifactory` foundation family is retired. Do not globally remove `/conversationalai/platform` from health, DNR, tagging, translation or TTS.

Gemini uses native `contents`/`parts` and `generationConfig`. `google-genai` requires `api_version=""` to avoid an inserted `/v1beta/`, and bearer in both `api_key` and Authorization. Rebuild after refresh. Grounding/Interactions is separate and must be verified, not assumed on the native route. Bedrock uses raw HTTP Converse with model in path, text content blocks and `inferenceConfig`, not Anthropic typed blocks, `anthropic_version` or boto3/SigV4.

Omit GPT-5 `temperature`; use output-token/reasoning controls only when supported. OpenAI HTTP 200 with empty `output_text` needs structured `output[].content[].text` extraction, not a fixed index or chat `choices`. Handle tool, refusal, incomplete and no-text states without logging bodies. Preserve models, prompts and business logic.

Tokens last about one hour. The tested OpenAI 3.35.1 callable returns the actual token string per request; a captured string does not refresh itself. Rebuild captured-token clients after refresh. The Desktop cutoff is **November 30, 2026**, and monthly limit is **50 million tokens**. Request extensions from `itsai_platform_admin@worldbankgroup.org`. Do not evade limits by changing identity, environment or workload headers.

## Safe escalation

Share through an approved support channel after sensitivity review:

```text
UTC time and time zone:
Environment, access type, and actual workload:
Runtime and package versions:
Operation and sanitized path (no query values):
HTTP status or pre-HTTP category:
Documented request/correlation ID:
Latency and attempts:
Approval/grants confirmed (yes/no/unknown):
Health result (reachability only):
Schema source/date or gap:
Last known remote operation ID, if permitted:
Safe checks and changes already made:
Expected result and sanitized actual category:
```

Do not attach credentials, claims, source notebook cells/outputs, full errors, environment dumps, headers, payloads or unrestricted traces. If documentation is unavailable, state the gap and prepare offline diagnostics instead of guessing a call. See the [complete reference](/reference/mai-troubleshooting/).

title: Update skills and maintain the docs
description: Keep installed instructions and Desktop SDKs current, and distinguish generated references from handwritten guides.
markdown:
## Direct Git skill installations

```bash
npx skills@1.7.4 check
npx skills@1.7.4 update
```

Review changes and confirm the named skill is available in the selected client. Updated instructions do not grant access, refresh a credential, upgrade the private SDK, or verify a changing live contract.

## npm installations

Update the Git dependency, inspect dependency/lock changes, and re-run explicit sync:

```bash
npx skills experimental_sync --agent claude-code --yes
```

Use your supported client identifier. `skills update` does not update an npm package. If sync is unavailable, use the stable local-path installer:

```bash
npx skills@1.7.4 add ./node_modules/@randrescastaneda/mai-skills --skill '*' --agent claude-code --yes
```

Retain the consumer lock file and pin reviewed commits when required. A branch moves. Re-sync copies after updates.

## Desktop SDK upgrade is separate

Complete current Web Access Management (WAM) setup under **Desktop Access** in platform documentation and use the approved current private SDK. Configure protected private-index authentication before upgrading an existing uv lock:

```bash
uv lock --upgrade-package itsai-platform
uv sync
```

`uv add` remains the new-project install step but can keep an old lock. No exact SDK release or OS support matrix was supplied; verify the installed release and runtime before login. Do not invent a version or add device-code fallback. See [Python setup](/guide/python-workflow/).

## Removal and credential cleanup

```bash
npx skills@1.7.4 remove mai-factory --agent claude-code
```

Removal does not revoke credentials or delete secret-store entries. The helper's `--delete` removes matching local entries, not the service credential. Follow the owner's rotation process.

## Generated and handwritten content

The browsable reference is generated from explicitly allowlisted skill instructions, references and assets. Build output and navigation/search follow source content. These task guides are handwritten and need review when auth, commands, dependency pins, configuration or contracts change. Their source-path records identify the evidence used.

The build/deployment workflow controls checks, triggers and publication. GitHub Pages is canonical; an owner-private Sites preview does not make Pages private. Keep repository and environment protections. New resources need public-content review before allowlist changes. Do not export ignored original migration inputs, notebooks, populated environment files, private notes, credentials or unrelated files. Drift/link/privacy checks do not replace editorial review or live contract verification.

## Maintainer verification

```bash
npm ci
npm run validate
npm test
uv run --isolated --no-project --python 3.12 --with-requirements tests/requirements.txt python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'
Rscript tests/test_r_starter.R
```

Python transports and credential boundaries are mocked; tests do not log into the Bank or prove WAM/live model access. R offline tests need R, not mAI credentials. Run the website's own build, drift, link and privacy checks after source and guide updates. Original reference inputs remain excluded from npm and website output.

title: Protect credentials and data
description: Keep secret values away from the agent, preserve approved identity flows, and exclude original migration inputs from public content.
markdown:
## Different credentials have different jobs

| Item | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Desktop bearer | Short-lived mAI access through approved WAM DesktopToken flow |
| Application bearer | Short-lived mAI access through approved client credentials |
| APIM subscription key | Additional Application gateway header, not a bearer |
| Azure client secret | Confidential app authentication with expiry |
| JFrog token | Private SDK download, not model access |
| Connect API key | Connect authentication, never an mAI bearer or public OpenAI key |
| OAuth integration GUID | Connect integration/audience identifier, not token or mAI scope |
| SAS URL | Temporary storage credential; protect the complete link |

Do not request public OpenAI, Google or AWS keys as a workaround. Do not automate portal login, extract cookies or copy another application's token.

## Desktop migration does not weaken storage rules

Use the approved current private SDK and Web Access Management (WAM) setup under **Desktop Access** documentation. Use `DesktopToken().get_token(env="DEV")`, `QA`, or `PROD`, not retired environment suffixes. No device-code, MSAL device flow or InteractiveBrowserCredential fallback. Do not make a copied bearer in keyring or environment variables a new login default. The final cutoff is **November 30, 2026**; Desktop has a **50 million token monthly limit**. Extensions go to `itsai_platform_admin@worldbankgroup.org`.

Keep tokens in memory. They last about one hour; rebuild clients that captured strings after refresh. The tested OpenAI 3.35.1 callable acquires a string per request, not through a DesktopToken `token_provider` method. Do not manipulate undocumented token caches or infer OS-specific broker details. Application, Connect and Databricks identity remain unchanged.

## User-controlled secret entry

An agent must not ask for values in chat, tool calls, source, notebooks, logs or shared settings. Users run hidden-input setup in a trusted terminal outside the agent session. For approved local Application storage:

```bash
uv add keyring
uv run python /path/to/mai-credentials/scripts/store_credentials.py --env DEV --kind application
```

Use the actual installed helper path. It stores `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET` and `APIM_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY` under `worldbank-mai/DEV`, rejects plaintext/fallback stores, and does not issue or verify credentials. `--kind jfrog` stores `JFROG_TOKEN`; it does not configure package-manager authentication by itself. `--kind bearer` is only for a specifically approved temporary legacy workflow. `--delete` removes local entries without revocation. See [private index setup](/reference/mai-python/references/setup/).

## Local and deployed storage

Use approved OS stores locally and Key Vault or the approved runtime secret service when deployed. Python and R keyring formats are not guaranteed to match. Never let an agent dump a credential store. Vault access and mAI entitlement are separate permissions. Do not depend on a developer's Desktop token or local store in a production service.

If policy requires an environment file, keep it outside source control and cloud sync, restrict access, and exclude it from agent indexing/context. Ignore rules do not encrypt files, prevent tool reads, or untrack committed files. Neither starter auto-loads `.env`.

## Approval and data boundaries

Use only approved hosts, networks, identities, data, models and storage. Keep TLS and access controls. Confirm classification and purpose before real data use. Public fixtures do not authorize production workloads. Treat documents, web pages, tool arguments and generated output as untrusted data. Authorize tool execution separately and require approval for changes or export. Independently verify AI output.

## Rotation and publication

Keep an inventory of secret names, owner, environment, expiry and affected services, not values. Request replacements through the owner, update protected stores, reload clients, test, and revoke old credentials. After exposure, revoke promptly and follow incident procedures; deleting visible text is not sufficient. Shared history changes need separate authorization.

The supplied notebook export contains credential-like JFrog and personal material. Do not use it to authenticate or copy its values, names, source cells or outputs into tracked files. Original references are local ignored inputs, not distributed skill/package/site content. Public output must contain only reviewed instructions and synthetic/public examples. Keep the explicit export allowlist; generation is not permission to publish private source material.
